title: 电感的记忆性：有初始电流时加恒定电压
statement: 电感 L = 2 H 在 t = 0 时已有电流 i_L(0) = −3 A（即实际电流 3 A 从下往上流过电感，参考方向见图）。从 t = 0 起，在电感两端加恒定电压 U_s = 6 V（t < 0 时 U_s = 0）。
求 t = 0.5 s 时的 i_L 和电感吸收的功率 p_L，以及 t = 2 s 时的 i_L；再求 t = 0 和 t = 1 s 时电感的储能，说明这段时间里储能如何变化。

questions.ask: t = 0.5 s 时电感吸收的功率 p_L = ?
questions.explain: p_L = u_L·i_L = 6 × (−1.5) = −9 W。功率为负：电感在向电源释放能量。
i_L(2) = −3 + 3 × 2 = 3 A。电流在 t = 1 s 过零后改变了实际方向。

questions.ask: t = 0 时电感的储能 W_L = ?
questions.explain: W_L = ½·L·i_L² = ½ × 2 × (−3)² = 9 J——储能只与电流大小有关，与方向无关。

questions.ask: t = 1 s 时电感的储能 W_L = ?
questions.explain: i_L(1) = −3 + 3 × 1 = 0，所以 W_L = 0。0 < t < 1 s 期间 |i_L| 减小，p_L < 0，电感把 9 J 磁场能量全部还给电源；t > 1 s 后 |i_L| 增大，电感又开始储能。

hints: 电感的积分关系：i_L(t) = i_L(0) + (1/L)∫₀ᵗ u_L(ξ) dξ——别忘了初始电流。
u_L 恒为 U_s，积分就是 U_s·t：i_L 随时间线性变化，斜率为 U_s/L，从 i_L(0) 出发。
储能 W_L = ½·L·i_L² 只和电流大小有关，与电流方向无关。
solution: **1. 电流表达式。** 电感直接接在电源两端，u_L = 6 V（t > 0）。由 i_L(t) = i_L(0) + (1/L)∫₀ᵗ u_L dt：i_L(t) = −3 + 3t A。
**结论：** 电感电流取决于全部“历史”（初始值 i_L(0) 记录了 t < 0 的作用），这就是电感的记忆性；同一电压下，电感是吸收还是释放能量取决于 u、i 的符号是否相同。

en.title: Inductor memory: constant voltage on an inductor with initial current
statement: At t = 0 the inductor L = 2 H already carries i_L(0) = −3 A (an actual current of 3 A flowing upwards through it; reference direction as drawn). From t = 0 on, a constant voltage U_s = 6 V is applied across the inductor (U_s = 0 for t < 0).
Find i_L and the power p_L absorbed by the inductor at t = 0.5 s, and i_L at t = 2 s; then find the stored energy at t = 0 and at t = 1 s and see how it changes in between.

questions.ask: Power absorbed by the inductor at t = 0.5 s, p_L = ?
questions.explain: p_L = u_L·i_L = 6 × (−1.5) = −9 W. The power is negative: the inductor is giving energy back to the source.
i_L(2) = −3 + 3 × 2 = 3 A. The current crosses zero at t = 1 s and then reverses its actual direction.

questions.ask: Energy stored in the inductor at t = 0, W_L = ?
questions.explain: W_L = ½·L·i_L² = ½ × 2 × (−3)² = 9 J — the stored energy depends on the size of the current, not its direction.

questions.ask: Energy stored in the inductor at t = 1 s, W_L = ?
questions.explain: i_L(1) = −3 + 3 × 1 = 0, so W_L = 0. During 0 < t < 1 s |i_L| shrinks and p_L < 0: the inductor returns all 9 J of magnetic energy to the source; after t = 1 s |i_L| grows and it stores energy again.

hints: Integral form of the inductor law: i_L(t) = i_L(0) + (1/L)∫₀ᵗ u_L(ξ) dξ — don't forget the initial current.
u_L is the constant U_s, so the integral is just U_s·t: i_L changes linearly with slope U_s/L, starting from i_L(0).
The stored energy W_L = ½·L·i_L² depends only on the size of the current, not its direction.
solution: **1. Current.** The inductor is connected directly across the source, so u_L = 6 V for t > 0. From i_L(t) = i_L(0) + (1/L)∫₀ᵗ u_L dt: i_L(t) = −3 + 3t A.

**4. Energy.** W_L(0) = ½ × 2 × (−3)² = 9 J, W_L(1) = 0, W_L(2) = 9 J. The inductor releases 9 J during 0–1 s and absorbs 9 J again during 1–2 s. Check: ∫₀¹ p_L dt = ∫₀¹ 6(−3 + 3t) dt = 6 × (−1.5) = −9 J ✓.

**Conclusion:** the inductor current depends on the whole history (the initial value i_L(0) records the effect of everything before t = 0) — the inductor has memory. Under the same voltage, whether it absorbs or releases energy depends on whether u and i have the same sign.
